confirmed.summary: Rules selected by `tag` or `max_count`/`min_count` (and types `require`/`limit`) are accepted by validate and counted by policy-coverage but can never produce a violation, so `policy` reports 'All N policy rules passed' rc=0 for a config those rules forbid.
confirmed.repro: resource with tags:[prod]; policies: [{id:t1,type:deny,tag:prod,...},{id:t2,type:limit,resource_type:file,max_count:0,...}]; forjar validate; forjar policy --no-color > o 2>&1; echo rc=$?; cat o; forjar policy-coverage --no-color
confirmed.observed: validate rc=0; policy rc=0 'All 2 policy rules passed.'; coverage 'Rules: 2 total, 0 triggered, 2 untriggered' with the tag rule counted under 'By resource scope: *'. Adding a condition_field/condition_value deny rule DOES fire (rc=1). Reproduced in 2 fresh dirs.
confirmed.expected: validate accepts these fields (it rejects genuinely unknown ones) and coverage counts them in scope, so the engine claims to evaluate them.
confirmed.root_cause: The evaluator implements only condition_field/condition_value for deny/warn/assert; the tag selector and count predicates used by limit/require have no evaluation branch.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Implement tag selection and max_count/min_count aggregate evaluation, make require/limit first-class in the evaluator, with a fixture per (type × selector).

confirmed.summary: `lint --rules <FILE>` has zero observable effect — a nonexistent path, a real rules file and a directory give byte-identical output and rc=0; the file is never opened.
confirmed.repro: config with a task; rules file banning tasks; forjar lint --no-color > base.txt; forjar lint --no-color --rules /does/not/exist.yaml > a.txt; forjar lint --no-color --rules /tmp > b.txt; forjar lint --no-color --rules r.yaml > c.txt; md5sum base.txt a.txt b.txt c.txt; forjar lint -f nope.yaml; echo rc=$?
confirmed.observed: all rc=0, all md5 3076b22315162431a589212978c6ce3e; a DIRECTORY produces no EISDIR. Control: lint -f nope.yaml rc=1 'error: failed to read nope.yaml…'.
confirmed.expected: lint --help: '--rules <RULES> FJ-374: Custom lint rules from YAML file'.
confirmed.root_cause: The option is parsed but no custom-rule loader/evaluator exists; only built-in + bashrs checks run.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Load and parse the rules file (hard error on failure), evaluate against resources, merge findings, exit non-zero on severity: error.

confirmed.summary: `logs --gc` claims a '10 runs/machine' retention but deletes an arbitrary subset — in two trials it deleted the 2nd-newest run and kept the oldest.
confirmed.repro: 15 applies with sleep 0.4 between; ls -1tr state/local/runs > order.txt; forjar logs --gc --dry-run | grep 'would delete' | sed 's#.*local/##;s/ .*//' > del.txt; map each to its index in order.txt
confirmed.observed: Trial A (13 runs): deleted oldest-first indices 3, 6, 9 — keeping #1/#2 (the oldest). Trial B (15 runs, fresh dir): deleted indices 2 5 14 12 4 — #14 is the 2nd-newest. Both rc=0 'Log garbage collection: deleted N runs'.
confirmed.expected: logs --help: '--gc Garbage-collect old logs'; the command's own message says 'within retention: 10 runs/machine', i.e. keep the 10 newest.
confirmed.root_cause: Run directories are enumerated in filesystem/hash order and the first N encountered are kept; no sort by timestamp precedes the retention cut.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Sort runs by start timestamp descending, keep the first N, delete the rest; test with 15 known-ordered runs.

confirmed.summary: `stack-diff` prints 'No differences found' ("total": 0) for two configs whose name and policy.failure differ — it only diffs params/machines/resources.
confirmed.repro: a.yaml (name alpha, policy.failure stop_on_first) vs b.yaml (BRAVO, continue_independent); diff a.yaml b.yaml; forjar stack-diff a.yaml b.yaml --no-color; echo rc=$?; forjar stack-diff a.yaml b.yaml --json; forjar validate -f a.yaml; forjar validate -f b.yaml
confirmed.observed: diff shows both changes; rc=0 '  No differences found.'; JSON {"diffs":[],"total":0}; validate 'OK: alpha' vs 'OK: BRAVO'. Control: a params-only change is reported ('+ z (Number(1))', '1 difference(s)').
confirmed.expected: stack-diff --help: 'FJ-1389: Unified stack diff — compare two configs'. policy.failure materially changes apply behaviour.
confirmed.root_cause: The differ walks only params/machines/resources; top-level scalars and the policy block are never compared.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Diff the full deserialized config generically (serde_yaml::Value trees) or add explicit comparisons for name/version/description/policy/outputs/environments/dist.

confirmed.summary: `rollback --dry-run -m <machine>` ignores -m and previews changes on ALL machines, while the real `rollback --yes -m` honours it.
confirmed.repro: git repo, 2-machine config, commit1 old1(m1)/old2(m2), commit2 new1/new2; forjar apply --yes; forjar rollback -m m1 --dry-run --no-color; forjar rollback -m m1 --yes --no-color; ls *.txt; forjar rollback -m bogusmachine --dry-run | tail -1
confirmed.observed: dry-run rc=0: '+ old1 …' AND '+ old2 …' / 'Dry run: 4 change(s) would be applied.'; real run rc=0 'm1: 1 converged' — old1.txt exists, old2.txt does not. -m bogusmachine gives the same 4-change preview.
confirmed.expected: rollback --help: '-m, --machine <MACHINE> Target specific machine', '--dry-run Show what would change without applying'.
confirmed.root_cause: The dry-run branch renders the git config diff before the machine filter is applied; only the execution branch passes -m down (and -m is not validated).
confirmed.fix_sketch: Apply the machine filter to the change set once, before the dry-run/apply branch, and validate the machine name.

confirmed.summary: `forjar migrate > out.yaml` (the documented default) appends a 'Migration complete:' line AFTER the YAML document, producing a config forjar itself refuses to load, while exiting 0.
confirmed.repro: config with a docker resource; forjar migrate > migrated.yaml 2>/dev/null; echo rc=$?; tail -1 migrated.yaml; forjar validate -f migrated.yaml; echo rc=$?; forjar migrate -o viao.yaml; forjar validate -f viao.yaml; echo rc=$?
confirmed.observed: migrate rc=0; last line 'Migration complete: 1 resource(s) converted, 1 warning(s)'; validate rc=1 "unknown field 'Migration complete' at 'Migration complete'"; the -o form validates rc=0.
confirmed.expected: migrate --help: '-o, --output <OUTPUT> Write migrated config to file (default: stdout)'; the 'Migration warnings:' block already goes to stderr.
confirmed.root_cause: The completion summary is printed with println! unconditionally instead of to stderr / only on the -o path.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Send the summary to stderr; test that migrate's stdout round-trips through `validate` rc=0.

confirmed.summary: `trigger <rulebook>` exits 0 reporting '1 action(s) fired' / "fired": true while the rulebook's apply action never runs — no resource converged, no state.
confirmed.repro: forjar.yaml with f1; forjar-rules.yaml rulebook rb1 with actions: [apply: {file: forjar.yaml}]; forjar rules validate; forjar trigger rb1 > t 2>&1; echo rc=$?; cat t; ls f1.txt state; forjar trigger rb1 --json; forjar apply --yes; ls f1.txt
confirmed.observed: rules validate 'Validation passed.'; trigger rc=0 'Trigger rb1: 1 action(s) fired' / '[0] apply'; f1.txt and state/ do not exist; --json {"rulebook":"rb1","fired":true,"actions_count":1}; forjar apply in the same dir DOES create f1.txt. Reproduced in 2 fresh dirs.
confirmed.expected: trigger --help: '--dry-run Dry-run: show what would fire without executing' — the non-dry-run form is meant to execute (and prints a different banner).
confirmed.root_cause: The non-dry-run path enumerates and counts matched actions but never dispatches them to an executor.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Execute each action and derive fired/actions_count from actual executions; propagate action failures to a non-zero exit.

confirmed.summary: `promote -t <env>` without --dry-run exits 0 with 'Result: APPROVED' / "all_passed": true but applies nothing and records no promotion history.
confirmed.repro: config with environments dev/prod and prod.promotion{from: dev, gates:[validate], auto_approve: true}; forjar promote -t prod < /dev/null > p 2>&1; echo rc=$?; tail -2 p; ls f1.txt state; forjar environments history prod
confirmed.observed: rc=0 'Result: APPROVED (auto-approve: true)' (--json "all_passed": true); f1.txt and state/ absent; 'No history for environment prod'. --dry-run produces identical gate JSON. Reproduced in 2 fresh dirs.
confirmed.expected: The tool's own dry-run footer says 'Dry-run complete. Use without --dry-run to apply promotion.' and --dry-run is documented as 'evaluate gates without applying'.
confirmed.root_cause: promote implements only gate evaluation; the apply-and-record stage after APPROVED is missing, so both modes are the same code path.
confirmed.fix_sketch: After gates pass, run the target environment's apply and append a promotion event; exit non-zero if that apply fails.

confirmed.summary: `forjar run <task>` executes the command with {{params.*}} unexpanded and reports 'status: pass', while `apply` resolves them; `run --param KEY=VALUE` has no effect.
confirmed.repro: config params:{who: alice}, task greet: echo "hello {{params.who}}" > out.txt; forjar apply --yes; cat out.txt; rm out.txt; forjar run greet; cat out.txt; rm out.txt; forjar run greet --param who=bob; cat out.txt
confirmed.observed: apply -> 'hello alice'. run rc=0 'command: echo "hello {{params.who}}" …' / 'status: pass'; out.txt -> 'hello {{params.who}}'. With --param who=bob: still 'hello {{params.who}}'. On the sandbox config `run marker-task` -> rc=1 "touch: cannot touch '{{params.sandbox}}/marker'".
confirmed.expected: apply resolves the same template on the same resource; run --help documents '--param <KEY=VALUE> Parameter overrides (key=value)'.
confirmed.root_cause: `run` reads the resource from the raw parsed config and shells out, bypassing the template/param resolution stage apply and show use; --param is parsed into an unused map.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Resolve the config with the param overrides before selecting the task, then generate and execute the script from the resolved resource.

confirmed.summary: `run <task> --json` exits 0 printing the command/script without executing it — and on a failing task the plain form exits 1 while --json exits 0.
confirmed.repro: forjar run side-effect; ls effect.txt; rm effect.txt; forjar run side-effect --json > b 2>&1; echo rc=$?; cat b; ls effect.txt; forjar run boom > o 2>&1; echo rc=$?; forjar run boom --json > o2 2>&1; echo rc=$?; cat o2
confirmed.observed: plain rc=0, effect.txt created. --json rc=0 {"task":…,"command":…,"script":…,"timeout_secs":null}, effect.txt absent. boom plain rc=1 "error: task 'boom' failed with exit 3"; boom --json rc=0, same shape, no status/success field.
confirmed.expected: run --help lists '--json  JSON output' — an output format, not a mode change.
confirmed.root_cause: The --json branch returns after serializing the resolved task descriptor, short-circuiting execution and exit-code propagation.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Execute first, then serialize {task, command, exit_code, status, stdout, stderr, duration}, propagating the text path's exit code.

confirmed.summary: `image --user-data` exits 0 reporting 'Wrote user-data' but the cloud-init file is not parseable YAML: a shell heredoc body sits at column 0 inside a `|` block scalar.
confirmed.repro: sandbox config; forjar image -m local --user-data -o ud.yaml > o 2>&1; echo rc=$?; python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('ud.yaml'))"; awk 'NR>=27&&NR<=31{print NR"|"$0}' ud.yaml
confirmed.observed: rc=0 'Wrote user-data for local to ud.yaml'; yaml.scanner.ScannerError at line 29 column 1 / 'could not find expected :' line 30; 27|'    - |' 28|'      cat > …<<'UNIT'' 29|'[Unit]' 30|'Description=Forjar First Boot Convergence'. Reproduced in 2 fresh dirs.
confirmed.expected: image --help: '--user-data Generate user-data only (for manual ISO build or PXE)'. cloud-init user-data must be valid YAML; the same generator feeds the --base ISO path.
confirmed.root_cause: Embedded multi-line heredoc content is interpolated without re-indenting each line to the block scalar's indentation.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Add an indent_block(text, n) helper used for all embedded multi-line content and test the output through a YAML parser.

confirmed.summary: `validate --check-resource-names PATTERN` matches the 'regex' as a literal substring — '.*' flags every resource — and exits 0 despite printing violations.
confirmed.repro: config with good-name and Bad_Name; for p in '.*' '^[a-z-]+$' 'Bad_Name'; do forjar validate --check-resource-names "$p"; echo rc=$?; done; forjar validate --check-naming; echo rc=$?
confirmed.observed: '.*' rc=0 'Resource naming violations (2): Bad_Name…; good-name…'; '^[a-z-]+$' rc=0 both flagged; 'Bad_Name' rc=0 only good-name flagged. Control --check-naming rc=1 with 'error: 1 naming violations'.
confirmed.expected: validate --help: '--check-resource-names FJ-745: Enforce resource naming regex pattern'; sibling --check-naming/--check-permissions exit 1 on violations.
confirmed.root_cause: The pattern is applied with name.contains(pattern) rather than a compiled regex, and the violation count never feeds the exit code.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Compile with the regex crate (error on invalid pattern), use is_match, exit 1 when violations exist.

confirmed.summary: `oci-pack` creates nothing (no dir, no blobs, no index.json) yet exits 0; --json suppresses its own 'not implemented' notice and emits a manifest as if it succeeded.
confirmed.repro: mkdir src; echo x > src/a.txt; forjar oci-pack src --tag t:1 > out 2>&1; echo rc=$?; cat out; ls; forjar oci-pack src --tag t:1 --output $D/myout; ls $D/myout; forjar oci-pack src --tag t:3 --output $D/j --json; ls $D/j
confirmed.observed: rc=0 with 'OCI layout generation requires sha2+flate2 crates.'; no oci-output/ and no --output dir created; --json rc=0 emits a full OCI manifest (schemaVersion 2, layers[], annotations) with no caveat while the dir does not exist. `forjar build` on the other hand writes a real layout with sha256 blobs.
confirmed.expected: oci-pack --help: 'FJ-2101: Pack directory into OCI image layout', '--output <OUTPUT> Output directory for OCI layout [default: oci-output]'. The stated reason is false — build proves those crates are compiled in.
confirmed.root_cause: oci-pack is a stub returning Ok(()); the --json renderer serializes a synthesized manifest before the stub's caveat is printed.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Implement on top of the working build layout writer, or exit non-zero with the caveat in both text and JSON.

confirmed.summary: `import --addr <unreachable>` spends ~15s failing to connect, then prints 'Imported 0 resources' and exits 0, writing a config for a machine it never reached.
confirmed.repro: time forjar import --addr 192.0.2.1 --user noah --scan packages,files,services -o out.yaml > o 2>&1; echo rc=$?; cat o; forjar import --addr 198.51.100.7 --user noah -o out2.yaml; echo rc=$?; forjar import --addr 127.0.0.1 --user noah --scan packages -o p.yaml   # control
confirmed.observed: rc=0 after 15.07s 'Imported 0 resources from 192.0.2.1 → out.yaml' (RFC5737 TEST-NET); same for 198.51.100.7. Control against localhost: 'Imported 1 resources' with a real package list.
confirmed.expected: import --help: 'Import existing infrastructure from a machine into forjar.yaml'.
confirmed.root_cause: Per-scan transport errors are swallowed into an empty resource list; connection failure is not distinguished from 'nothing to import'.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Probe connectivity up front and abort rc=1 on failure; otherwise propagate scan errors and exit non-zero when every scan failed.

confirmed.summary: `plan -m` filters only the printed body — summary counts and --json stay unfiltered (unknown machine: empty body next to '3 to add') — and `plan-compact -m` has no effect at all, even for a nonexistent machine.
confirmed.repro: 2-machine config; forjar plan -m m1; forjar plan -m m1 --json | python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d['to_create'],[c['resource_id'] for c in d['changes']])"; forjar plan-compact > pc0; forjar plan-compact -m m1 > pc1; diff pc0 pc1; forjar plan-compact -m does-not-exist; forjar plan -t nosuchtag | sed -n '1p;$p'
confirmed.observed: plan -m m1 body shows only r1 but summary 'Plan: 2 to add…'; --json to_create=2 changes=['r1','r2']. plan-compact -m m1 byte-identical to unfiltered; -m does-not-exist prints the whole plan rc=0. On the single-machine config `plan -m ghost` shows an empty body with '3 to add' while `apply -m ghost` converges 0. Control `plan -t nosuchtag` -> 'Planning: two-m (0 resources)' / '0 to add'.
confirmed.expected: Both --help texts document '-m, --machine <MACHINE> Target specific machine'; the tag filter shows the correct behaviour.
confirmed.root_cause: In plan, -m is applied inside the per-machine print loop rather than to the change set feeding counters/JSON; in plan-compact the option is parsed and unused. Neither validates the machine name.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Filter the change list once after planning and derive body/summary/JSON from it in both commands; error on an unknown machine.

confirmed.summary: `apply --yes --preview` and `--output-scripts DIR` exit 0 having applied nothing and written no state, and --preview never shows a generated script — it prints a plan.
confirmed.repro: forjar apply --yes --output-scripts ./sc > o1 2>&1; echo rc=$?; ls sc|head -3; ls *.txt; test -d state; rm -rf state sc; forjar apply --yes --preview > o2 2>&1; echo rc=$?; head -2 o2; forjar status; echo rc=$?
confirmed.observed: --output-scripts rc=0 'Exported 9 scripts to ./sc' then a plan; no .txt, no state. --preview rc=0 prints only 'Planning…' + plan (no script text); no .txt, no state. status rc=1 'cannot read state dir state'.
confirmed.expected: apply --help: '--preview FJ-360: Show generated scripts before execution' (execution implied to follow) and '--output-scripts FJ-365: Write generated scripts to directory for manual review'.
confirmed.root_cause: Both options short-circuit apply into the planner and return Ok(()); --preview reuses the plan renderer instead of the script generator --output-scripts already has.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Make --preview print the generated scripts then proceed with the apply; for --output-scripts, either continue or print an explicit 'apply skipped'.

confirmed.summary: `plan` names the file it will create as literal '{{params.sandbox}}/a.txt' in text, --json and --why; `show` resolves it correctly.
confirmed.repro: forjar plan | sed -n '1,4p'; forjar plan --json | python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['changes'][0]['description'])"; forjar show -r a-file | grep path; forjar apply --yes; ls a.txt
confirmed.observed: '  + a-file: create {{params.sandbox}}/a.txt'; json same; show 'path: /tmp/.../a.txt'; apply creates the resolved path. plan --why compounds it: '- path changed: /tmp/.../a.txt -> {{params.sandbox}}/a.txt'.
confirmed.expected: show --help: 'Show fully resolved config (recipes expanded, templates resolved)' — that path is what apply writes; plan is the pre-flight review surface.
confirmed.root_cause: The plan renderer formats descriptions from the raw parsed config; apply and show use the resolved config.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Resolve the config once at the top of plan and render descriptions/diffs from the resolved resources.

confirmed.summary: `show -r <resource>` emits YAML where the resource name is a null-valued key and the fields are its siblings, so the document does not describe the resource.
confirmed.repro: forjar show -r a-file > r.yaml 2>&1; echo rc=$?; cat r.yaml; python3 -c "import yaml;print(repr(yaml.safe_load(open('r.yaml'))))"; forjar show | sed -n '/^resources:/,/mode/p'
confirmed.observed: rc=0; 'a-file:' then 'type: file' … at indent 0; parses to {'a-file': None, 'type': 'file', 'machine': 'local', 'path': …, 'mode': '0644'}; full show nests them two levels under resources:/a-file:. (`show -r a-file --json` is correct.)
confirmed.expected: show --help: 'Show fully resolved config'; the full output is the authority on the shape.
confirmed.root_cause: The -r renderer prints the name then serializes the body at indent 0 instead of serializing a single-key map.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Serialize BTreeMap{name: resource} with serde_yaml; test that the output yaml-parses to a mapping under the resource name.

confirmed.summary: `validate --json` emits plain text instead of JSON whenever validation fails — the one case a consumer needs the structured result.
confirmed.repro: config referencing an unknown machine; forjar validate --json > out 2>&1; echo rc=$?; cat out; python3 -m json.tool < out; fix the machine ref; forjar validate --json; echo rc=$?
confirmed.observed: rc=3 'error: validation errors:\n  - resource r1 references unknown machine ghostmachine' -> not JSON. Valid config: rc=0 {"valid": true, …, "errors": []}. Same plain text for YAML parse failures (rc=3).
confirmed.expected: validate --help: '--json Output validation result as JSON'; the success payload already carries an `errors` array.
confirmed.root_cause: Validation errors return Err before the JSON renderer runs, and the top-level handler prints text regardless of --json.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Render {"valid":false,"errors":[…]} when --json is set, keeping the non-zero exit.

confirmed.summary: `validate --schema-version <anything>` reports OK for nonsense versions — the value is never checked.
confirmed.repro: for v in 99.0 not-a-version '' 0.0.0-bogus; do forjar validate --schema-version "$v" > o 2>&1; echo "[$v] rc=$? $(cat o)"; done
confirmed.observed: all four rc=0 'OK: v (1 machines, 1 resources)' for a config declaring version "1.0".
confirmed.expected: validate --help: '--schema-version <SCHEMA_VERSION> FJ-381: Validate against specific schema version'; `status --format bogus` shows the right pattern ('error: unknown format …' rc=1).
confirmed.root_cause: The option is parsed but never compared against the config's declared version or a known-version table.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Reject unknown versions and fail when the requested schema does not accept the config's declared version.

confirmed.summary: `history --resource <name>` prints 'No event logs found.' rc=0 although the event log exists and holds that resource's events.
confirmed.repro: apply twice with changed content; grep -c a-file state/local/events.jsonl; forjar history | head -2; forjar history --resource a-file > out 2>&1; echo rc=$?; cat out; forjar history -m local --resource a-file
confirmed.observed: 4 a-file mentions; plain history prints started/complete lines; --resource a-file rc=0 'No event logs found.'; with -m local the same.
confirmed.expected: history --help: '--resource <RESOURCE> FJ-357: Show change history for a specific resource'; `forjar audit` shows ResourceStarted/ResourceConverged for a-file.
confirmed.root_cause: With --resource set the reader switches to a per-resource log path forjar never writes, instead of filtering events.jsonl.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Filter the machine event logs by the resource field; reserve the 'no event logs' message for a genuinely missing state dir.

confirmed.summary: `import --addr <ip>` without -n derives the machine key and hostname from the first octet ('192', '198'), and `--scan <unknown-category>` is accepted silently, yielding an empty config plus a success message.
confirmed.repro: forjar import --addr 198.51.100.7 --user noah -o out.yaml; sed -n '3,10p' out.yaml; forjar import --addr 198.51.100.7 --user noah -n edge01 -o out2.yaml; sed -n '3,10p' out2.yaml; forjar import --addr 127.0.0.1 --user noah --scan totally-bogus-category -o z.yaml; forjar import --addr 127.0.0.1 --user noah --scan packages -o p.yaml
confirmed.observed: name: imported-198, machines: '198: {hostname: 198, addr: 198.51.100.7}'. With -n edge01 it is correct. --scan totally-bogus-category rc=0 'Imported 0 resources' (empty resources:); --scan packages rc=0 'Imported 1 resources' with a real list.
confirmed.expected: import --help: '-n, --name <NAME> Machine name (used as key in machines section)' and '--scan <SCAN> What to scan [default: packages,files,services]'; the generated config is meant to be applied.
confirmed.root_cause: Default name is addr.split('.').next() (fine for FQDNs, wrong for IPv4), and unknown scan tokens are dropped instead of erroring.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Use the full address (sanitized) or require -n when the addr is an IP; validate every --scan token and error on unknown ones.

confirmed.summary: `test --sandbox <backend>`, `--pairs` and `--mutations N` all produce output structurally identical to a plain run, and --sandbox accepts values outside its documented set without error.
confirmed.repro: 3-resource applied config; base=$(forjar test --json); for a in '--sandbox bogusbackend' '--sandbox chroot' '--pairs' '--mutations 0' '--mutations 500'; do compare forjar test --json $a against base ignoring duration fields; done
confirmed.observed: all five == base; result set is always the 3 per-resource check results; no pairwise or mutation result ever appears; the invalid backend produces no error or warning.
confirmed.expected: test --help: '--sandbox <SANDBOX> Sandbox backend: pepita, container, chroot [default: pepita]', '--pairs Enable pairwise preservation matrix (convergence tests)', '--mutations <MUTATIONS> Max mutations per resource'. Compare `forjar completion powershell` rc=2 with a possible-values list.
confirmed.root_cause: test runs only per-resource check scripts; the pairwise/mutation engines are never invoked and the sandbox backend is neither validated nor used.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Make --sandbox a clap value_enum and dispatch on it; run/report pairwise and mutation results, or reject the flags explicitly.

confirmed.summary: `test -r <unknown-resource>` exits 0 with an empty table and 0 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip, so a typo turns the test gate into a silent green.
confirmed.repro: forjar test -r nosuch --no-color > o 2>&1; echo rc=$?; cat o; forjar test -r nosuch --json; forjar test -t nosuchtag | tail -1; forjar explain nosuch; echo rc=$?
confirmed.observed: rc=0, empty table, '0 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip'; --json {"pass":0,"fail":0,"skip":0,"results":[]} rc=0; -t nosuchtag -> '0 pass, 0 fail, 3 skip'; explain nosuch rc=1 "error: resource 'nosuch' not found".
confirmed.expected: `explain` on the same unknown name is the binary's own convention (rc=1 'not found').
confirmed.root_cause: -r filters without a membership check and an empty result set is reported as a pass.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Validate -r against the config's resource ids (rc=1) and treat an empty selection as an error.

confirmed.summary: `graph --stats` reports 'Density: 0.80' while `graph --density` reports '0.2000 (4 edges / 20 max, 5 nodes)' for the identical graph.
confirmed.repro: 5-node config (base->mid1, base->mid2, mid1->leaf, mid2->leaf, island); forjar graph --no-color --stats; forjar graph --no-color --density
confirmed.observed: --stats 'Nodes: 5  Edges: 4 … Density: 0.80'; --density 'Graph density: 0.2000 (4 edges / 20 max, 5 nodes)'. Both rc=0, stable.
confirmed.expected: graph --help: '--stats FJ-424' and '--density FJ-779: Show graph density (edges / max-possible-edges)'; --density shows its arithmetic and is right for a 5-node directed graph.
confirmed.root_cause: --stats computes edges/nodes instead of edges/(n*(n-1)).
confirmed.fix_sketch: Have --stats call the --density function; unit-test both on a known graph.

confirmed.summary: `graph --prune NOSUCHRES` exits 0 claiming 'Pruned NOSUCHRES and 0 dependent(s)' and `--highlight NOSUCHRES` is silently ignored, while sibling resource-taking flags error 'not found'.

confirmed.summary: `graph --highlight` / `--prune` emit mermaid edges in the opposite direction from the default view and --edge-list, without --reverse.

confirmed.summary: `diff -r <resource>` filters the rows but not the summary counts, so `-r NOSUCH` prints an empty list beside 'Diff: 0 added, 1 removed, 1 changed' (JSON "diffs": [] beside "removed": 1).

confirmed.summary: `anomaly` reports 'No anomalies detected' for a resource that failed 3 of 6 applies and for a 130x duration outlier, and `--min-events 9999` still analyzes every resource.

B) durations 0.033,0.033,0.032,0.032,0.031 then 4.033 -> 'No anomalies detected'. confirmed.summary: `state-rm --force` ('Skip dependency check and force removal') has no effect — the unforced form already removes a resource another resource depends_on, with the same message and exit code.

confirmed.summary: `bench --compare` never reads a baseline — missing, valid, or a directory at benchmarks/RESULTS.md all give output structurally identical to running without the flag.

confirmed.summary: `bench --iterations 0` divides by zero to print 'NaNµs', marks all six targets FAIL / '✗ 0/6 targets met', and still exits 0.

confirmed.summary: `fmt` (and `lint --fix`) rewrites the config in place through a YAML round-trip that discards every comment, with no warning and no backup.

confirmed.fix_sketch: Use a comment-preserving YAML round-trip, or refuse to rewrite a commented file without --force and write a .bak.

confirmed.summary: `rolling --batch-size 0` and `parallel-apply --max-parallel 0` panic ('chunk size must be non-zero') and abort with exit 134 instead of rejecting the value.

confirmed.summary: `logs` reports a different run ID for the same apply than history/audit/state-query, so a run ID copied from those into `logs --run` yields 'No run logs found.'

confirmed.summary: `logs --resource <name>` suppresses ALL per-resource lines — output for an existing resource is byte-identical to a nonexistent one.

confirmed.summary: `logs --script` is byte-identical to `logs` — the .script sidecars are 0 bytes and the transport log's SCRIPT section is empty, so there is nothing to show.

confirmed.summary: `logs --follow` prints 'Press Ctrl+C to stop' then exits in ~5 ms without streaming, and ignores --run (always watches the newest run).

confirmed.summary: `state-query <q> --churn` is byte-identical to the unflagged command in text and JSON, while sibling enrichment flags each add a section.

confirmed.summary: `forjar template` emits the input verbatim — no template is expanded, even {{params.*}} which `show` resolves — and `-V/--var` is recorded in the --json 'vars' object but never applied; a value with no '=' is accepted silently.

confirmed.summary: `contracts -f <missing|malformed|directory>` prints a clean coverage report and exits 0 instead of reporting the config could not be read.
confirmed.repro: forjar contracts -f $D/absent.yaml; echo rc=$?; forjar contracts -f bad.yaml; echo rc=$?; forjar contracts -f adir; echo rc=$?; forjar contracts -f absent.yaml --json; forjar complexity -f absent.yaml; echo rc=$?; forjar impact -f absent.yaml -r x; echo rc=$?

confirmed.summary: `forjar saga` prints 'Success: true' / "success": true rc=0 while every step is Pending, nothing is applied, and the snapshot files it names are never created.

confirmed.observed: rc=0 'Saga Execution Plan' / 'Stacks: 1 | Applied: 0 | Failed: 0 | Compensated: 0' / 'Success: true' / '[PENDING] dogfood-sandbox'; the named snapshot path does not exist; no state/ and neither resource created; JSON {…"status":"Pending"…,"applied":0,"success":true}.

confirmed.summary: `environments rollback <env>` exits 0 ('Rollback logged') with zero generations to roll back to, restores nothing, fabricates an audit event, and accepts --generations 0 as success.

confirmed.root_cause: It writes a rollback_triggered event and returns Ok without locating or restoring a generation, and does not validate --generations.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Resolve the target generation first, error if missing or --generations<1, restore, then log the event.

rejected.summary: `apply --force` (and `rollback --yes`) restores a tampered file or creates a missing one but reports '0 actual change(s), N forced no-op(s)' in both the note and the JSON summary.
rejected.repro: forjar apply --yes; echo TAMPERED-CONTENT > a.txt; md5sum a.txt; forjar apply --yes --force > out 2>&1; echo rc=$?; cat out; md5sum a.txt; cat a.txt; forjar apply --yes --force --json | python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['summary'])"
rejected.observed: a.txt 75ea83eb… -> 82c23ef4… ('TAMPERED-CONTENT' -> 'aaa'); rc=0 'note: --force re-ran 3 resource(s) the lock reported as unchanged (0 actual change(s), 3 forced no-op(s))'; JSON {'forced_noop_count': 3, 'actual_changes': 0}. Same note when `rollback --yes` CREATES a file that did not exist.
rejected.expected: The artifact demonstrably changed, so it was not a no-op; the note's own wording is the spec, and `drift` reports the same resource DRIFTED.
rejected.root_cause: 'actual change' is classified from the pre-apply lock comparison rather than the observed before/after state, so live drift and creations count as forced no-ops.
rejected.fix_sketch: Classify from the handler's own result (applied hash vs observed pre-state hash) and count creations as changes.
rejected.resolution: NOT A DEFECT — intended, contract-specified behaviour. Moved from confirmed 2026-08-23. contracts/apply-summary-distinguishability-v1.yaml defines forced_noop_count(cfg) = if cfg.force then shadow_plan(config, real_locks).unchanged else 0 — LOCK-based, deliberately — with the invariant forced_noop_count + actual_changes = total_converged, which the reported numbers satisfy (0 + 3 = 3). Both counts answer 'how many did --force re-run that the LOCK called unchanged', which is cheap and deterministic; 'how many have live drift' is what `forjar drift` answers. Conflating the two was the ORIGINAL bug: a previous fix subtracted live drift here and was REVERTED as a regression (GH-208; FJ-129 shape 4 went 2 -> 1). What WAS wrong is the wording: '0 actual change(s)' read as 'nothing on the machine changed' when it meant 'nothing differed from the lock'. The message now says what it measured and points at `forjar drift` for the live question. Fixed as a phrasing defect; the count is unchanged by design.
